statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The 22:00 UTC futures restart produced a contained 59-point NQ range on thin volume with no adverse weekend gap, so the observed price path shows none of the shallow-pullback, failed-retracement or session-extreme structure that defines mean-reversion failure, and Tail remains far below the block threshold. Stress stays elevated on a restrictive Treasury curve, a stretched energy complex and an active Iran-US maritime conflict with an Iranian prohibited zone signalled but not yet declared.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk stays concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC thin-liquidity window rather than across the whole outlook, and every forecast hour maps below the block threshold; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures reopened at 22:00 UTC in a contained 59-point range on thin volume, with no adverse weekend gap despite the verified Iran-US Navy exchange and an undeclared Iranian prohibited zone
body: CME equity index futures reopened at 22:00 UTC for the first time since Friday, and this is the first Claude assessment of the week with a live Nasdaq-100 price path. The observed restart is orderly rather than disorderly. NQ front-month last printed 29,565.25 inside a 29,535.25-29,594.25 session range on roughly 2.15k contracts, a span of about 59 points or 0.2%, and ES traded 7,722.00 inside a 7,715.50-7,723.75 range on about 2.36k contracts. Against Friday's Nasdaq-100 cash close of 29,544.15 that is effectively flat, so the adverse weekend gap that the closed-venue hours had flagged as the main conditional risk did not materialise. Quoted change and percentage fields on both futures still carry Friday's session values at this cutoff, so the last price, the session range and the volume are treated as the observed evidence and the reopen change itself is not asserted. Tail is scored on that contained path: there is no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after a failed retracement, and no hold near a session extreme, which are the structures that define mean-reversion failure. Tail therefore stays far below the block threshold. Cross-asset evidence supports the same reading. VIX last closed at 14.53 after a 13.80-14.58 Friday range, which is not a stressed equity-volatility regime. Gold was lower on the latest session rather than bid, so there is no broad safe-haven rotation. Latest-session internals were rotational rather than aligned: semiconductors were higher across the board while five of eight Nasdaq megacaps fell, and index futures diverged, with Nasdaq-100 firmer while S&P 500 and Dow futures were softer. That split argues against a one-way regime being carried into the new week. Stress nevertheless stays elevated, and the reasons are unchanged. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for September 3 shows the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.25%, a restrictive curve into a September 15-16 FOMC that sits outside this outlook window. The energy complex is stretched, with WTI near $92.22 and Brent near $96.87 after a roughly 8-9% weekly gain, and US diesel has been reported at a record $5.85 per gallon on the combination of Iran-related disruption and constrained refining. OPEC+ met on Sunday and left October quotas unchanged, pausing the unwinding of the 1.65 million barrel-per-day cut after six consecutive monthly increases, with the next meeting on October 4. The geopolitical picture remains a live two-way maritime conflict. Following the verified weekend exchange in which the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at US warships and US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers, Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran will declare a prohibited zone beginning at the US Navy blockade line and extending toward Hormuz and into the Gulf, with any identified vessel placed on Iran's sanctions list. Verified reporting confirms the zone has been signalled but not yet declared, so it remains a conditional driver rather than observed evidence. It is also an incremental escalation rather than a new closure, because the Strait of Hormuz is already described as effectively closed with shipping traffic sharply reduced since fighting began on February 28, which caps the marginal supply shock a declaration could deliver. Conditional risk in this outlook is therefore concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC window, where a headline discontinuity would meet the thinnest order book of the week, and that window still maps below the block threshold because gap risk without observed extension after a failed retracement is not evidence of mean-reversion failure. Monday September 7 is the US Labor Day holiday: US cash equity, ETF and listed options markets are closed for the full day, CME equity index futures trade a shortened session that halts at 17:00 UTC, and the US data calendar is empty until Tuesday. The five closed hours from 17:00 to 21:00 UTC return Tail to the closed-venue floor by construction. The next scheduled US items are the NFIB survey and the New York Fed consumer expectations release on Tuesday, ahead of PPI and Oracle results on September 10 and CPI on September 11.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Across the available hours Tail held a flat 5, with a single 4, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress climbed from 56 through a 52-60 band to finish the window at its high of 60 as the Sunday geopolitical flow accumulated. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every available hour, reflecting a closed venue rather than an observed regime.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the newly reopened Sunday session, a full Asian and European session on the US Labor Day holiday, a shortened US futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, and five closed hours before the restart. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band for every hour, peaking at 15 in the pre-Tokyo liquidity trough where a headline discontinuity would meet the thinnest book of the week, easing through Asia and Europe, and returning to the closed-venue floor of 5 once futures halt for the holiday break. Stress starts at 57, holds in the low-to-mid 50s through the European and notional US hours, and unwinds toward 49 during the closed hours. Confidence decays from 85 to 64 across the window as live evidence gives way to conditional assumption. No US macro release falls inside the window; the next scheduled items are Tuesday's NFIB and New York Fed expectations releases, ahead of PPI on September 10 and CPI on September 11.
